Lieutenant General Mirghani Idriss Suleiman is an officer of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Director-General of Defense Industry System (DIS), a company subject to restrictive measures by the European Union for providing support to actions and policies that threaten the peace, stability and security of Sudan. In 2026, he was appointed as Assistant for Military Industries Affairs within the SAF.
DIS is described as Sudan’s largest defence enterprise, generating an estimated USD 2 000 000 000 in revenue through hundreds of subsidiaries across various sectors of Sudan’s economy. DIS manufactures a range of small arms, conventional weapons, ammunition and military vehicles for the SAF.
As the Director-General of DIS, Mirghani Idriss Suleiman has travelled extensively with General Abdelfattah Al-Burhan, Commander-in-Chief of the SAF, since the beginning of the war, allegedly, to enhance the SAF’s capabilities to fight the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on several fronts in Khartoum, Darfur and Kordofan.
Therefore, Mirghani Idriss Suleiman provides support to actions or policies that threaten the peace, stability or security of Sudan.
Function: Lieutenant General in the SAF; Director-General of Defence Industries System; Head of Sudanese Army Production Agency; Assistant for Military Industries Affairs within the SAF
Associated individuals: General Abdelfattah Al-Burhan, Commander-in-Chief of the SAF
Associated entities: Defense Industry System, SMT Engineering; SAF

Mustafa Ibrahim Abdel Nabi Mohamed is a former senior official of the Sudanese Central Bank, seconded since 2017 to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), to serve as a Financial Director, and helping it to manage a web of proxy companies and entities.
A UN Panel of Experts Report on sanctions in Darfur referred to a former senior official of the Sudanese Central Bank who is based in Dubai and has become the RSF’s financial adviser without naming him. The report also explains that al Khaleej Bank became instrumental to the RSF’s financing in 2019 when its majority ownership was acquired by individuals and entities associated with the RSF.
Media reports and think-tanks have identified that person as Mustafa Ibrahim Abdel Nabi Mohamed. He is a Director of Al Khaleej Bank, a Sudanese bank.
Over 60 % of the shares of Al Khaleej Bank are held by companies associated with the family of Mohammad Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti), the head of the RSF.
Mustafa Ibrahim Abdel Nabi Mohamed is also the majority shareholder of Shield Protective Solutions Co. Ltd. The other shareholder in that company is one of the brothers of Hemedti, Musa Hamdan Dagalo Musa, and the company holds over 14 % of the shareholding in al Khaleej Bank.
In 2026, he is identified as being part of a network linked to the leadership of the RSF, which has amassed a vast property portfolio in Dubai as part of a sprawling “paramilitary-industrial complex” across Africa and the Middle East. It is in this context that he purchased a high-end apartment in the Burj Khalifa, a skyscraper in Dubai, demonstrating that he benefits from the conflict in Sudan.
As a Financial Director of the RSF, Mustafa Ibrahim Abdel Nabi Mohamed is engaging directly or indirectly in providing support to, or benefitting from, actions or policies that threaten the peace, stability or security of Sudan.
Function: Director of al-Khaleej Bank; majority shareholder of Shield Protective Solutions Co. Ltd. (Sudan); Financial Director of the RSF
Associated individuals: Musa Hamdan Dagalo Musa, brother of RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo
Associated entities: Al-Khaleej Bank; Shield Protective Solutions Co. Ltd. (Sudan)

Abu Aqla Mohamed Ahmed Kaikal is a Sudanese Military Commander who served in the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Gezira State in Sudan until he defected to the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) in October 2024.
Since 2025, Abu Aqla Mohammed Kaikal is the Leader and Commander of the Sudan Shield Forces, an armed group that fights alongside the SAF. On 12 December 2025, he appeared in a video threatening civilians attempting to flee El Obeid City in North Kordofan State, which was under siege by the RSF. In the video, he is heard warning that civilians who attempted to leave the city would be shot.
The Sudan Shield Forces played a major role in the fighting in Gezira State and in the East Nile district, in the Khartoum area. On 10 January 2025, the Sudan Shield Forces intentionally targeted civilians and their property in an attack.
Therefore, Abu Aqla Mohamed Ahmed Kaikal is responsible for actions and policies that threaten the peace, stability and security of Sudan. In addition, he is responsible for directing acts in Sudan that constitute serious human rights violations, and for obstructing the delivery of, access to and distribution of humanitarian assistance in Sudan.
Function: Leader and Commander of the Sudan Shield Forces, a SAF-affiliated militia
Associated entities: SAF
